about: Which pieces of the client templates the new WSL distribution wires, decided from the definitive manifest (evidence/artifacts/new-wsl-definitive-defaults-20261001/definitive-manifest.json). tools/adoption/new_wsl_client_config.py reads this file. Each entry has `match`, a list of patterns over piece keys (fnmatch: * is any text; the keys are listed by `new_wsl_client_config.py --check`), and one `wiring`: `slot:<foundation slot id>` (the piece is wired while the manifest says that slot installs something and its default names `owner`; otherwise it is not wired and says why), `practice` (repository practice that needs no tool outside the repository; a hook of this kind may run only python3, jq and the shell's own words, which the recipe's F4 installs and adoption/bootstrap-linux.sh requires, and only files that tools/adoption/install_claude_profile.py copies), `not_wired:<reason>`, or `authorization:<reason>` (a setting that grants a permission or suppresses a confirmation: Claude Code permissions.defaultMode and skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt, Codex approval_policy and sandbox_mode, and the Codex tool approval modes `default_tools_approval_mode` (any value) and `approval_mode` when it approves; it is neither rendered nor written unless --with-authorization-settings is given, and then never over a value the file already has; an entry may also name a `slot` and its `owner`, and the piece is then written only while that slot installs the owner, as the tool approval modes of an MCP server are; the tool refuses such a setting classed practice or slot). A piece goes to the first entry that matches it, so a specific entry stands before a general one. A piece no entry matches, and an entry that no piece reaches, fail the check. `names` lists how the tool appears in templates and instruction text; `--check` renders the example host, without and with --with-authorization-settings, and fails when a rendered file or an instruction block holds the name of a piece that is not wired. `override` replaces the piece's value (for an MCP server, the keys it names); `rewrite` replaces text inside a string value, and `{gateway_port}` is the install plan's port; `home_dir` is a directory under the home that a wired path piece adds to PATH. Sources: adoption/bootstrap.md steps 2, 4 and 4a; adoption/bootstrap-linux.sh (full_profile_* functions, install_native); docs/decisions/2026-10-02-new-wsl-client-configuration.md. `keep_existing` (a Claude setting only) writes the template's value only when the host's settings.json has no value for it. `dependent_sentences` declares a sentence of an instruction block that depends on the one before it on its line (`starts` is its opening words, `on` is always `previous`): the block filter drops it whenever that sentence goes, and the dropped list shows it. The dependency is declared here, never inferred.

dependent_sentences.starts: Check relevance; retry without pin priority
dependent_sentences.why: It refines the ai-memory query the sentence before it describes ('pin priority' is that query's `pin_first`), so without that sentence it points at nothing to check or retry.
